free_tier.stated: 'Up to $200 in free credits' on the pay-as-you-go plan, with 'Tier 0 | Free | 10' concurrent sandboxes. The page does not say what 'up to' depends on, and no expiry is stated.
free_tier.notes: Credits are topped up to raise the tier; the free grant is bounded by a qualifier the page never explains.

per_object_cap.stated: No per-sandbox vCPU or memory cap is published on the pricing page; the Custom plan advertises 'Up to 256 GB RAM per sandbox or job' as an upgrade over pay-as-you-go.
per_object_cap.notes: The binding cap is lifetime, not shape.

retention.stated: Sandboxes sit 'on automatic standby' with memory and filesystem snapshotted; Tier 0 and Tier 1 'enforce expiration dates (Tier 0 and 1, with respectively up to 7 and 30 days)'. In higher tiers unlimited persistence is permitted.
retention.notes: Seven days at Tier 0 is the hard ceiling on how long one sandbox can exist.

egress.terms: No egress charge is listed; outbound traffic can be constrained by a per-domain firewall and a proxy, which is a policy control rather than a meter.

limits.value: 'Up to $200 in free credits', qualifier unexplained
sandbox expiry at Tier 0 is at most 7 days
outbound can be restricted to a domain allowlist through the proxy

limits_note: Every sandbox scales to zero after inactivity whether or not an expiry policy is set, so 'running' is not a state Blaxel holds by default.

identity_cost.detail: Signup is 'Start for free' with no card shown on the pricing page; no hold is mentioned. Raising the tier requires a top-up, which introduces a card at that point.

reliability_note: 'Automatic scale-to-zero after 5s inactivity' means a process with no client connection is suspended unless keep-alive is arranged; the docs offer process keep-alive as the workaround.
confidence_note: The credit, the rates and the tier-0 expiry are first-party. What is not established: whether a keep-alive process suspends the 5-second standby timer in practice, and whether Tier 0 counts the 7-day limit from creation or from last wake.

evidence.proved: 'Up to $200 in free credits. Spin up your first sandbox in under a second.' and 'Because Blaxel scales sandboxes to zero the second they're idle and resumes the full memory state in just 25 milliseconds' and '$0 compute costs on standby' and 'Up to 256 GB RAM per sandbox', quoted
'Every account starts with free-tier quotas. As you top up credits, your tier automatically increases.', quoted; the page lists no dollar credit

quoted: 'Up to $200 in free credits', 'Access to all Blaxel products', 'Tier 0 | Free | 10' sandbox limit, and the rate 'Active CPU ... $0.0000115 / GB RAM · second' with '$0 compute costs on standby'.

quoted: 'Some quota tiers enforce expiration dates (Tier 0 and 1, with respectively up to 7 and 30 days). In higher tiers, unlimited persistence is permitted.'; 'the automatic standby (scale-to-zero) which happens to all sandboxes when inactive'.
quoted: 'Automatic scale-to-zero after 5s inactivity, resume from standby under 25ms even after weeks.'

quoted: 'Sandboxes stay active as long as there's an active connection to them'; 'You can also use process keep-alive to keep the sandbox running when you launch a process, even if there isn't an active connection to it.'

notes: Blaxel prices CPU inside the RAM rate: USD 0.0000115 per GB of RAM per second is USD 0.0414 per GB-hour, so a 1 GB sandbox is USD 0.0414 an hour and USD 200 would be 4,831 hours, or a 4 GB sandbox USD 0.1656 an hour and 1,208 hours. Neither number is reachable as a month of uptime because of the 7-day Tier 0 expiry and the 5-second standby. The borrow against it: it is the cheapest per GB-hour of the sandbox providers here, and the right tool for bursty agent work.

extras.billing_model: per-second on active CPU, keyed to RAM

session_cap.note: 7-day maximum sandbox existence at Tier 0; standby after 5 s without a connection

network_out.ports: exposed TCP ports and preview URLs

ps.price: on standby the compute is $0; disk is not priced on this page
ps.durability: full memory state is preserved across the suspend
ps.retention: the page states no retention limit on a suspended sandbox

extras.price_arithmetic: 0.0000115 x 3600 = 0.0414 per GB-hour; 1 GB x 730 = 30.22; 200 / 0.0414 = 4831 h theoretical, capped by the 7-day expiry

binding_note: A 7-day maximum existence beats the credit: USD 200 cannot buy a month because no single sandbox is allowed to live that long at Tier 0.
